stories.headline: Houthi attacks disrupt Riyadh flights as Saudi-led coalition prepares a new Yemen operation

sources.body: Qatar’s emir says ‘efforts must be doubled’ to restore maritime navigation in the Gulf and the Strait of Hormuz.
sources.headline: Child among five civilians killed by Houthis in Yemen’s Taiz province

sources.body:
Unidentified projectile strikes King Khalid airport, killing one and injuring 11, as escalating attacks threaten to draw more countries into Yemen conflict

Analysis: attack will force rethink of Trump strategy

A projectile hit a passenger terminal at the airport in Riyadh on Sunday, the day after a deadly missile attack on the facility carried out by Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthi rebel group killed 13 people.

An unidentified projectile hit terminal 4 at King Khalid international airport, starting a fire, killing one person and injuring 11, according to Saudi civil aviation authorities. Air defences also intercepted a cruise missile in the vicinity of the airport. It was the latest of several attacks on the airport in the past week.

The escalating attacks threatened to draw more countries into the Yemen conflict and further widen the regional fallout of the US-Iran war, which has already spread to Lebanon and Iraq.

In a post on X, the British embassy in Saudi Arabia advised against all but essential travel to the cities of Jeddah and Dammam and to avoid almost all airports.

After Saturday’s strike on Riyadh airport, the US president, Donald Trump, said he was weighing whether to join the Saudi military campaign in Yemen, telling reporters: “We’re going to look into it.”

The Iran-allied Houthis claimed to have launched several attacks on the airport, including the attack on Saturday, which killed 13 people and injured more than 300 – the deadliest attack on a Gulf country since the war with Iran started in March and an apparent escalation in the Houthis’ war with Saudi Arabia and the Yemeni government that Riyadh sponsors.

In response to the attack, Saudi authorities extended the closure of the airport and said schools would be moved online until Thursday.

The Houthis claimed that Saudi Arabia struck the airport in Yemen’s rebel-held capital, Sana’a, on Sunday, without providing more information on damage or casualties.

Videos circulated on social media showing travellers walking through debris-strewn ground in the Riyadh airport as sirens blared. Four Saudi citizens, two Bangladeshi nationals, a Palestinian, a US citizen, an Egyptian, a Jordanian, a Syrian and a Sudanese were killed in the missile strike.

On Sunday evening, Saudi authorities also confirmed King Fahd international airport in the eastern city of Dammam had been attacked, with the country’s civil aviation authority saying on X: “The assessment of the damage and verification of the safety of airport facilities were still under way, in coordination with the relevant authorities.”

On Saturday night, the spokesperson for the Saudi-led coalition in Yemen, Maj Gen Turki al-Maliki, said the coalition would “respond firmly” to the attack, offering few other details.

The Houthis said a Saudi airstrike on Sana’a on Sunday hit a home and killed a child, as well as injuring six others.

The Houthis doubled down on their threats on Sunday, warning airlines, passengers and staff to stay away from Saudi airports. The group said “the worst is yet to come” if Saudi military action in Yemen continued.
sources.headline: Riyadh airport hit again after deadly Houthi missile attack, Saudi authorities say

sources.body: Flights to and from Riyadh have been suspended following deadly Houthi attacks, with several international airlines extending cancellations through October 19. The disruption threatens Saudi Arabia’s ambitions to become a major global aviation hub, while Delta has postponed its first direct US flights to the Kingdom until March 2027.
sources.headline: Airlines suspend flights to Riyadh amid security fears

stories.headline: Drone attack sinks a ship off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast, prompting diplomatic fallout with Russia

sources.body:
Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev has summoned the Russian ambassador after two merchant ships were struck by drones off Bulgaria's Black Sea coast.

Eleven crew members are missing and one sailor was saved, according to local officials, after one of the vessels sank 17 nautical miles (31km) east of the village of Krapets.

The other vessel, Ukrainian owned, was hit by drones 18 nautical miles from the town of Byala and all 15 crew were rescued.

The attacks come a week after two other commercial ships were hit by sea and aerial drones in Bulgaria's exclusive economic zone. One of the ships, the Alfa Watan, sank and all 10 crew, including nine Syrians, are presumed dead.

Radev convened an emergency meeting on Tuesday and said he had summoned Russian envoy Eleonora Mitrofanova. Although there was no conclusive evidence of blame on "either side... the logic suggests that the outcome benefits the Russian Federation", he said.

Mitrofanova was later quoted by Bulgarian media as telling Radev she had no information from Russia's defence ministry relating to the latest attacks. She also said these strikes could have been a provocation by a third party.

Bulgaria is a Nato member, and Radev also spoke to secretary general Mark Rutte about the latest attacks.

"Nato will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea," Rutte said after the talks.

"We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed," he added.

The two ships were struck just outside Bulgarian territorial waters.

If this had happened just a few nautical miles to the west, Article 5 of the Nato treaty could have been triggered. The article defines an armed attack on one member of the military alliance as an attack on all.

Radev had earlier asked Nato and the EU for technical assistance in investigating the previous attacks that took place on 6 October, indicating it was unclear who was behind them.

Radev came to office during the summer and has since rejected suggestions that he is "pro-Russian".

Ukraine has directly blamed Russia for the latest attacks and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen spoke on Tuesday of the Black Sea becoming "another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine. This is unacceptable".

Russia's military has not publicly commented on the issue. It has recently intensified its strikes on vessels in the Black Sea, particularly the western side, as part of its war against Ukraine.

The same day that two ships were targeted off Bulgaria last week, Ukraine hit an oil tanker in the Russian Black Sea port of Sochi.

Moscow says it is targeting ships delivering weapons and dual-use cargo to Ukrainian ports - and cited attacks in the ports of Mykolaiv and Chornomorsk last week, along with one in the Black Sea.

However, Kyiv and its European allies say merchant vessels carrying grain and other civilian cargo are being attacked.

Meeting with his security chiefs on Tuesday, Bulgaria's prime minister said: "Another attack on merchant ships in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters is absolutely unacceptable".
sources.headline: Bulgaria summons Russian ambassador after ship sinks in Black Sea drone attack

sources.body:
Two ships were hit in the attack, including the Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which sustained damage.

Two ships have been hit in drone attacks off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, with one of them sinking, Prime Minister Rumen Radev said.

The Ukrainian-owned Chelsea 3, which was sailing under a Maltese flag, was hit by three drones and damaged about 18 nautical miles (33km) off Bulgaria at about 1:30am on Tuesday (22:30 GMT on Monday), Radev said.

Radev said its 15-man crew, seven of them Ukrainians and eight Azerbaijanis, was rescued. Five crew members received medical assistance, and no one was seriously injured.

He added that one crew member from the ship that sank was also rescued.

Radev called the incident “absolutely unacceptable”.

“Another attack in the immediate vicinity of Bulgarian territorial waters,” he said in a televised address.

Radev also said there was no clear evidence of who carried out the attack, but “the outcome benefits” Russia and that the Russian ambassador would be summoned over the incident.

As a member of the NATO military alliance, Bulgaria holds a strategic position on the Black Sea, where Russia and Ukraine have vital ports.

European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen condemned the attack on the ships.

“The Black Sea has become another front of escalation of the Russian war in Ukraine,” she said.

“This is unacceptable. I strongly condemn the drone attacks on merchant ships near Bulgaria’s coast. Putting the lives of the crew in grave danger and threatening security in the Black Sea,” she wrote on X.

“We stand with Bulgaria and thank its rescuers for their swift response. Those responsible should be held accountable,” von der Leyen added.

NATO chief Mark Rutte said the alliance would adjust its defences “as needed” following the incident.

“NATO will continue to work closely with our allies in the Black Sea. We have already strengthened our posture along the eastern flank and will continue to monitor the security environment, adjusting our deterrence and defence posture as needed,” Rutte said on X after talking to Radev.

The incident comes as concerns grow over hybrid attacks involving Russia.

Last week, drones hit two ships off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast , causing one to sink. All 10 crew members from the ship that sank remain unaccounted for .
sources.headline: Drone attack sinks ship off Bulgaria’s Black Sea coast, PM says

stories.headline: IMF upgrades global growth outlook but warns war, debt, inflation and AI valuations threaten resilience

sources.body:
World Economic Outlook says states’ oil stocks are low and budgets are overstretched, as it upgrades UK GDP growth forecast for 2026

Threat of AI share crash puts world financial stability at risk, says IMF

The global economy “could soon test the limits of resilience”, as emergency oil stocks run low and government budgets become overstretched, the International Monetary Fund has warned.

In its twice-yearly World Economic Outlook, the IMF said global growth had withstood the Middle East conflict better than feared over the past six months.

It said the rerouting of oil supplies away from the strait of Hormuz, and the release of strategic energy stocks, had helped to contain the impact on oil prices from the US-Iran war.

However, it warned that emergency stocks are now depleted, and high debt levels and deficits in many countries could leave governments with little capacity to protect consumers from any future jump in prices.

“Without shoring up supply capacity and replenishing policy buffers, the global economy could soon test the limits of resilience,” it said. “Inventories in energy markets are dwindling and additional geopolitical shocks could still transmit rapidly through prices and supply disruptions.”

The International Energy Agency announced the largest-ever emergency releases of oil stocks on to the market in March this year, and promised to accelerate it after a meeting of oil ministers last month .

But in a sign of the system’s vulnerability, the US strategic petroleum reserve was recently reported to have fallen to its lowest level since 1982.

Last week, Donald Trump agreed a deal with Vladimir Putin to temporarily lift sanctions on US imports of Russian diesel in an attempt to bring down prices at the pumps, which analysts said would have little “meaningful” effect.

The World Economic Report was published on Tuesday in Bangkok, where the IMF and World Bank are holding their annual meetings this week, with finance ministers and central bankers scheduled to attend.

Launching the report in Bangkok, Silvana Tenreyro, the IMF’s economic counsellor, said “the global economy has been resilient, but that resilience is reaching its limits”. She urged policymakers to “move from just coping, to rebuilding”.

Ahead of the gathering, the IMF managing director, Kristalina Georgieva, urged governments to tighten their belts , amid rising global debt levels. “We cannot keep delaying necessary policy action – you have the tools, now have the wisdom to use them,” she said.

In the report, the IMF revised up its forecast for global economic growth this year marginally, to 3.1% – against 3% in its last update in July. Next year’s forecast is unchanged, at 3.4%.

US growth remains unchanged at 2.3% this year and revised up to the same pace, 2.3%, for 2027 – from 2.2% at the last update.

The IMF predicted GDP growth of 1.3% for the UK this year – up 0.3 percentage points from its most recent update in July – in welcome news for the chancellor, John Healey, who is poised to arrive in Bangkok later this week.
sources.headline: IMF warns global economy ‘could soon test the limits of resilience’

sources.body: The IMF has raised its 2026 global growth forecast slightly to 3.1%, citing the resilience of advanced economies despite rising energy prices caused by the Iran war. But it warned that poorer countries that are not benefiting from the AI boom remain particularly vulnerable to energy shocks, economic uncertainty and mounting debt.
sources.headline: IMF upgrades 2026 global growth forecast but war and debt threaten outlook

stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV is hospitalized for surgery to remove an early-stage lung nodule

sources.body:
Leo arrived at hospital on Tuesday for the surgery, which is deemed low risk and could take place this afternoon

Pope Leo has been admitted to hospital in Rome for an operation to remove a small growth from his lung, a discovery a top Vatican cardinal said had come “like a bolt out of the blue”.

In a rare moment of Vatican transparency, Leo, 71, said during his angelus prayer on Sunday that doctors had found a small nodule on his lung during a check-up , adding that it was “well-contained” and detected early.

“The doctors believe it would be right to intervene and so, following their advice, I have decided to have the operation to remove it,” he said to the crowds gathered in St Peter’s Square.

Leo, who in May last year became the first US-born leader of the Roman Catholic church, is being treated in Rome’s Gemelli hospital, where a large crowd greeted the pontiff.

The Vatican has not disclosed the timing of the operation, although it could take place on Tuesday afternoon, according to Italian media reports. All of his appointments have been cancelled until 20 October.

Cardinal Pietro Parolin, the Vatican secretary of state, said he had seen Leo on Monday night. “We spoke with great serenity,” Parolin told Rai News . “He is truly a great example. The announcement came like a bolt out of the blue, nobody expected it. Thank God it was detected immediately, so the operation could take place immediately. Normally, when these things are caught in time, they can be resolved.”

The operation is deemed low risk and will determine whether the nodule is malignant.

Leo will stay in the 10-floor private-patient wing but not in the papal suite, which is being renovated.

The Chicago-born pope, who enjoys sports, especially playing tennis, is generally believed to be in good health. He often makes use of the papal retreat in Castel Gandolfo, close to Rome.

Leo travelled to France on a papal visit in September and is scheduled to go to South America in November for a 12-day trip covering 10 cities.

A digest of the morning's main headlines from the Europe edition emailed direct to you every week day

The weekly papal audience on Wednesday will be led by Luis Antonio Tagle, a cardinal from the Philippines who last week was elected dean of the college of cardinals – the authority that presides over papal conclaves.

The Gemelli, located in the north-west of the Italian capital, is renowned for treating reigning popes. Pope John Paul II stayed there so many times that the Vatican worked with the hospital to establish the high security papal suite.

Leo’s predecessor, Francis, spent more than five weeks in the hospital, being treated for bronchitis which developed into bilateral pneumonia. He died at home in Casa Santa Marta in Vatican City on 21 April 2025, just under a month after being discharged.
sources.headline: Pope Leo admitted to hospital for operation to remove growth on lung

sources.body: Pope Leo XIV has been admitted to Rome’s Gemelli hospital for surgery to remove a small lung nodule discovered during recent medical checks. The 71-year-old pontiff said the growth was detected at an early stage. The procedure marks his first hospitalisation since becoming pope in May 2025. FRANCE 24's Seema Gupta has the latest from Rome.
sources.headline: Pope Leo XIV admitted to hospital for lung surgery

stories.headline: Cyberattack on French supermarkets spoils food in hundreds of stores

sources.body:
Hackers raise temperatures in fridges at hundreds of supermarkets, sparking fires and spoiling food in ‘large-scale’ cyberattack.

Cyberattack on French supermarkets causes fires, millions in losses

A cyberattack on refrigeration systems at hundreds of supermarkets in France has raised the temperature of fridges and freezers to as high as 50 degrees Celsius (122F), spoiling food and causing fires at several stores.

Top retailers Intermarche, Cooperative U, E Leclerc and others confirmed the “unprecedented” cyberattack on Monday.

At least 300 shops of Intermarche or its Netto brand were targeted, along with more than 100 Cooperative U outlets, the retailers told the AFP news agency.

Carrefour said 80 supermarkets were affected, while Monoprix said about 5 percent of its roughly 490 stores were hit. E Leclerc said several of its stores were targeted.

The Paris prosecutor’s office said the “large-scale” ⁠attack had affected “connected refrigerators in several major food retailers across France”. It led to food losses and fires, the office said.

The attack prompted Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu to order France’s National Cybersecurity Agency (ANSSI) to investigate, a person in his office told the Reuters news agency.

The source said France was coordinating with European counterparts because other countries could also be affected, adding that authorities were assessing whether other French companies were at risk.

There was no immediate estimate of industry-wide losses, but Intermarche CEO Thierry Cotillard told BFM TV the “unprecedented” attack would represent losses amounting to “tens of millions of euros nationwide in a single day”.

According to BFM TV, the hackers “managed to remotely trigger the forced defrosting of the refrigeration systems in numerous stores”. The action resulted in the “destruction of stocks of fresh and frozen products”, it said.

Intermarche told AFP that affected stores would have to “throw away all of the products” that were fresh or frozen.

Dominique Schelcher, chief executive of Cooperative U, said the attack had disrupted refrigeration systems since Sunday night.

“Targeting equipment essential to the preservation of fresh products and to the food supply of the French people is extremely serious and is unprecedented. It is unacceptable,” he wrote on X.

He said the company’s teams were working to restore normal operations as quickly as possible, and that an investigation would be needed to “shed full light on this attack”.

Supermarket cold aisles are typically run by control ⁠panels that manage an entire store’s fridges and freezers and can be accessed over the internet, which lets maintenance companies adjust them from anywhere.

The ⁠source close to Lecornu said ANSSI had identified a vulnerability in software supplied by Danish company Danfoss.

Danfoss said it was “aware of incidents in France affecting a limited number of refrigeration management systems”.

The affected units “were running outdated firmware”, the company said, adding that it had “long advised customers” to keep their systems updated and replace older equipment.
sources.headline: Hundreds of supermarkets in France hit by ‘unprecedented’ cyberattack

sources.body: Hundreds of supermarkets across France have been targeted in an unprecedented cyberattack that remotely altered the temperatures of fridges and freezers, causing large quantities of fresh and frozen food to spoil. Major retailers, including Carrefour, Monoprix, E.Leclerc and Coopérative U, were affected, with the Les Mousquetaires group reporting around 300 impacted stores. Losses could reach several million euros. The refrigeration systems involved used outdated software that no longer received security updates. Some fires were also reported, and French authorities have launched an investigation to identify those responsible.
sources.headline: Cyberattack hits hundreds of French supermarkets, spoiling millions of euros in food

stories.headline: Democrats make corruption and cost of living a central midterm message

sources.body: Democrats may be discovering the political power of calling something rigged. They’re leaning hard into anti-corruption messaging in the final weeks of the campaign as new research suggests that linking corruption to Americans’ economic struggles can boost Democrats into the home stretch. Messaging from Democrats that tied corruption to housing, health care and the cost of living increased voter support for Democratic congressional candidates by about 3 percentage points, according to a national survey last month conducted by Blue Rose Research and Democratic-aligned Winning Jobs Narrative Action, which was obtained by POLITICO . The findings align with a shift in how Democrats are talking about corruption — and help explain why that message has exploded on the campaign trail. From Sen. Jon Ossoff in Georgia to James Talarico in Texas and Abdul El-Sayed in Michigan, Democrats have zeroed in on a common argument: Washington is rigged to benefit the wealthy at the expense of everyday Americans. “We have a corruption crisis in this country, and it is leading to an affordability crisis,” Iowa Democratic state Rep. Josh Turek said during his Senate debate against Rep. Ashley Hinson last week. It’s a message that is reverberating across campaigns. In a recent presentation delivered to Democratic groups on Capitol Hill, longtime Democratic strategist Jesse Ferguson offered a succinct playbook: “Corruption is why your costs are high,” according to the presentation viewed by POLITICO. His presentation also encouraged Democrats to lead with the acknowledgement that costs are high and then go into corruption, acknowledge that it happens across parties and avoid making President Donald Trump the sole focus of their attacks. “Trump works as an example of corruption that raises costs, not as the whole case,” the presentation said. Since April, Democratic candidates and outside groups in House and Senate races have spent roughly $104 million on advertising mentioning corruption, according to ad tracking firm AdImpact. Republicans, meanwhile, have spent $36 million across House and Senate campaigns over the same period. “It’s not just like, ‘oh, look at what’s happening with the ballroom,’ or ‘boy, Donald Trump’s made a lot of money on crypto,’” Democratic strategist Chris Meagher said. "You have to be able to tie it to the impact on people’s lives." “The narrative works best when it’s an outsider candidate who is linking a rigged economy to a rigged political system,” longtime Democratic pollster Celinda Lake said of the anti-corruption messaging. Running against corruption is not new. But as Democrats looked for a way out of the political wilderness after 2024, they began turning a familiar attack — anti-corruption — into a broader message tied to voters’ economic pain. What once was an attack largely focused on Trump has become a more expansive argument for candidates trying to connect it to why Americans are struggling financially, potentially providing a blueprint for the party beyond November. “Democrats used to talk about corruption as a crime. Now corruption is the explanation for costs,” Ferguson, the Democratic strategist, said. The issue — and messaging around it — is also coming to the fore in a cycle when anger over the suppression of Epstein files hit a fever pitch and public pressure to ban Congress from trading stocks continues to mount. And it’s not just the research by Blue Rose that shows the potential potency of that message. In another recent survey from the Democratic group Navigator Research , obtained by POLITICO, the vast majority of Americans — both Democrats and Republicans — say corruption is driving up their costs. That same survey of registered voters, conducted in August, found majorities, including roughly a quarter of Republicans, say Trump is bringing more corruption to Washington than fixing it. And new results from the nonpartisan Center Square’s Voter Voice Poll, conducted this month by Noble Predictive Insights and shared first with POLITICO, show 10% of voters ranking government corruption as the second most important issue facing Americans, tied with the economy and jobs, and only behind inflation and price increases. In some instances, Democrats have wrested the word “rigged” away from Trump who has used it in the context of unproven election fraud and turned it into a mobilizing political talking point. That’s a departure from March 2024 when Democrats criticized then Rep. Katie Porter for accusing special interests of spending money to “rig” the California Senate race after she lost in the state’s primary. But now some Democrats are embracing that language as a way to rail against what they see as a corrupt system. “They’re rigging the rules to benefit their wealthy donors and corporate special interests,” former Ohio Democratic Sen. Sherrod Brown said in a message to supporters announcing the launch of his campaign to return to office. But the corruption resonates across parties. Republicans who spoke with POLITICO said Democrats do not own the issue — voters everywhere are animated by it. While polling shows that voters in both major parties believe the government is corrupt , Republicans accuse Democrats of lacking credibility on the issue. “Americans have been disgusted by the level of self-serving corruption that spread like herpes through the slimy politicians who run the Democrat Party, and now they’re suddenly changing their tune because it’s an election year,” National Republican Congressional Committee spokesperson Mike Marinella said in a statement. “Voters see through the facade, and they know Republicans are cleaning up the rot left behind by Democrat leaders.” On the Senate side, National Republican Senatorial Committee spokesperson Bernadette Breslin pointed POLITICO to a poll in Minnesota — a rare offensive opportunity for Senate Republicans this cycle — that shows there are just about as many voters who blame Democratic Gov. Tim Walz for widespread fraud of federally-funded government programs in the state as there are who blame the criminals. Walz’s lieutenant governor, Peggy Flanagan, is running for Senate against Republican Michele Tafoya, and corruption under Democratic rule is a key theme for Republicans in the race. “The overwhelming majority of Minnesotans blame the Walz-Flanagan administration — and the criminals it aided and abetted — for plundering their hard-earned taxpayer dollars,” Breslin said. “They’ll vote for Michele Tafoya to right the ship this November.” Steve Pierce, executive director at Winning Jobs Narrative Action, said one of the biggest shifts for Democrats this cycle on corruption has been a move away from a message largely rooted in concerns over democratic norms, which have struggled to break through in a way that moves voters in past cycles. “You’ve seen Democrats, rather than connecting corruption to democracy, connecting it to affordability, connecting it to the top concern that voters have,” said Pierce. “It’s connecting it in a way that’s meaningful to voters around the things that they are thinking about every day.” The anti-corruption message has played out across the country, and as an explanation for frustration against different economic pain points, including rising electric bills and local data center projects. A recent memo on data centers from House Majority PAC, the main super PAC working to elect House Democrats, noted the “message environment in the 2026 election cycle has been dominated by costs, with an important secondary theme around corruption that began to emerge last year.” The group’s spokesperson, CJ Warnke, told POLITICO that “every single poll and every single focus group shows affordability to be voters’ number one issue, and they specifically point to corrupt politicians as being responsible for driving up prices.” Next month’s midterms will offer the clearest test yet of whether Democrats can turn this message into votes. But Democratic operatives increasingly see anti-corruption messaging as more than just a short-term political weapon — as long as they try to do something about it if they win control next year. “I think the thing for Democrats, if they do want to keep it on the radar heading into 2028, and I think they should because I think it is a really potent issue for them, they are going to have to also deliver on it,” said Pierce. “They have to be able to show up to get caught trying,” he said.
sources.headline: Democrats are making corruption messaging a pocketbook issue

stories.headline: Spain's king and queen visit Ceuta amid migration pressures and renewed tensions with Morocco

sources.body: <p>Sin retirar a su máximo representante diplomático en Madrid ni emitir mensajes públicos de condena, como ocurrió en 2007 durante la <a href="https://elpais.com/diario/2007/11/06/espana/1194303603_850215.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/diario/2007/11/06/espana/1194303603_850215.html">visita de Juan Carlos I</a> a las ciudades autónomas norteafricanas, Marruecos recibe con silencio oficial la presencia de Felipe VI en Ceuta, este martes, y Melilla, al día siguiente. Pocas horas antes del inicio del viaje real, en la Embajada de España en Rabat se aguardaba la asistencia de altos cargos del Gobierno marroquí a la recepción ofrecida por la fiesta nacional del 12 de Octubre. Finalmente no acudieron en pleno proceso de formación del nuevo Gobierno de la primera ministra, Fátima Mansouri, quien anunció en la noche del lunes un pacto de coalición de centroizquierda.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-13/prudencia-en-marruecos-ante-la-primera-visita-de-un-rey-de-espana-a-ceuta-y-melilla-en-dos-decadas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Prudencia en Marruecos ante la primera visita de un rey de España a Ceuta y Melilla en dos décadas

sources.body:
Los reyes se han volcado este martes con los ceutíes en su histórica visita a la ciudad autónoma , que se produce dos meses y medio después de la entrada masiva de migrantes desde Marruecos . Felipe VI y doña Letizia han viajado a Ceuta para para mostrar su solidaridad y apoyo a los ceutíes tras la crisis migratoria.

Se trata de la primera visita a la ciudad autónoma desde que Felipe VI llegó al trono y la primera de un jefe del Estado desde 2007 , cuando sus padres, Juan Carlos I y doña Sofía, visitaron tanto Ceuta como Melilla.

En una conversación informal con los periodistas en la recepción de la Fiesta Nacional en el Palacio Real, Felipe VI aseguró este lunes estar muy "ilusionado" con este viaje a las ciudades autónomas -tras Ceuta, visitará también Meilla-. Además, en esta ocasisón, los reyes pernoctarán en Ceuta, algo que no ha ocurrido nunca antes en democracia, porque los eméritos no durmieron en ninguna de las ciudades autónomas.

A su llegada a la ciudad autonóma, los monarcas han sido recibido por centenares de ceutíes , a los que han ido saludando casi uno a uno de camino al primer lugar que iban a visitar: el Palacio de la Asamblea. Al contrario de otras visitas oficiales, Felipe VI y doña Letizia han estado saludando durante 20 minutos antes de entrar en el edificio, donde han sido recibidos por las autoridades.

La agenda de los reyes en Ceuta ha empezado con una visita al Ayuntamiento de Ceuta , donde han mantenido un encuentro con el Gobierno que encabeza el 'popular' Juan Jesús Vivas y donde han recibido las llaves de la ciudad.

En la recepción, Vivas ha dado las gracias a los reyes por acudir a la ciudad autónoma a "sembrar confianza donde más se necesita la confianza, confianza para resistir y confianza para alumbrar la salida del túnel".

El presidente ceutí ha repasado la historia de la ciudad y ha recordado que cuando se separaron los reinos de Portugal y España, "los ceutíes de entonces" eligiero quedarse con España. "Por tal motivo, el rey, Don Felipe IV, le concede a Ceuta el título de la Muy Noble, Leal y Fidelísima. Han pasado casi 400 años, y los ceutíes, con la visita de Sus Majestades, tenemos hoy la oportunidad de dar un nuevo testimonio de lealtad", ha sostenido.

Para este martes por la tarde, los reyes tienen prevista una visita al colegio de Educación Infantil y Primaria Vicente Aleixandre. También se desplazarán al cementerio de Sidi Embarek , donde habrá un acto homenaje de las alrededor de 140 personas que fallecieron cuando intentaban llegar a nado desde Marruecos a finales de julio. Muchos de ellos se encuentran precisamente enterrados en este cementerio musulmán, en tumbas sin nombre, ya que no todos han podido ser identificados.

Concluirán la jornada con un encuentro con la sociedad civil ceutí en el Parador de Ceuta , donde está previsto que el rey pueda dirigirse a los ceutíes.

Cuando se inició la crisis migratoria, Felipe VI calificó la entrada masiva de migrantes como "una "inaceptable violación" de una frontera española y europea . Su interés en la situción de Ceuta ha sido constante. El 6 de agosto recibió al presidente ceutí en Marivent, y tras ese encuentro, Vivas aseguró que el rey quería viajar a Ceuta.
sources.headline: Los reyes viajan a Ceuta para mostrar su solidaridad dos meses y medio despu�s de la entrada masiva de migrantes

sources.body: <p>La <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-supremo-mantiene-para-el-29-n-la-suspension-del-derecho-al-voto-de-los-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-supremo-mantiene-para-el-29-n-la-suspension-del-derecho-al-voto-de-los-nacionalizados-por-la-ley-de-nietos.html">suspensión del derecho al voto de los nacionalizados</a> por la <i>ley de nietos</i> confirmada este lunes por el Tribunal Supremo cierra la puerta a que este dé marcha atrás en su decisión tras el adelanto electoral, como habían pedido la Abogacía del Estado y la Fiscalía, y abre un sinfín de dudas sobre cómo va a poder llevarse a cabo esa medida sin precedentes. Los magistrados dejan su cumplimiento en manos de la Oficina del Censo Electoral y de los consulados que, ya antes de que se convocaran las elecciones generales para el 29 de noviembre, consideraban “materialmente imposible” culminar a tiempo para las elecciones autonómicas y municipales de mayo la revisión del Censo de Electores de Residentes Ausentes (CERA) que requiere la orden del Supremo. En sus autos de este lunes, la Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo ha acordado, además, ofrecer a los afectados (163.020 personas, según la Abogacía) personarse en el procedimiento en el plazo de cinco días, lo que puede derivar en un aluvión de recursos de difícil gestión a mes y medio de las elecciones.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-13/el-tortuoso-camino-para-aplicar-la-orden-del-supremo-sobre-la-ley-de-nietos-de-los-recursos-expres-a-las-revisiones-del-censo-fuera-de-plazo.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: El tortuoso camino para aplicar la orden del Supremo sobre la ‘ley de nietos’: de los recursos exprés a las revisiones del censo fuera de plazo

sources.body:
El Tribunal Suprem (TS) ha decidit mantenir la suspensió cautelar del vot per als nacionalitzats per l'anomenada llei de nets. Per tant, 163.020 persones que es van nacionalitzar com a descendents d'exiliats de la Guerra Civil no podran votar a les eleccions generals del 29 de novembre , el cens de les quals s'ha tancat aquest dilluns.

Així, la secció quarta de la sala contenciosa administrativa del TS ha desestimat les al·legacions de l'Advocacia de l'Estat contra la suspensió cautelar. Cinc magistrats s'han pronunciat a favor de la suspensió cautelar i només hi ha hagut un vot particular en contra d'una magistrada.

A parer d'aquesta magistrada, l'avançament electoral ha alterat "de manera substancial" el marc pel qual es va acordar inicialment la suspensió cautelar, fet que "obliga a efectuar una altra valoració". És a dir, considera que la mesura acordada converteix "en irreversible l'eventual lesió del dret de sufragi dels afectats".

Tant la Fiscalia com l'Advocacia de l'Estat havien demanat que s'aixequessin les mesures cautelars dictades el 10 de setembre al·legant que era impossible revisar els gairebé 170.000 expedients afectats pels recursos de Iustitia Europa i Vox.

Tanmateix, la sala ha considerat que "l'interès general de preservar la puresa del procés electoral ha de prevaler sobre el dret de sufragi" dels nacionalitzats per la llei de nets, inclosa dins la llei de memòria democràtica del 2022.

El govern espanyol ha lamentat la decisió del Tribunal Suprem (TS) i estudia si pot recórrer al Tribunal Constitucional. De moment, el PSOE ha acusat el líder del PP , Alberto Núñez Feijóo, i el de Vox , Santiago Abascal, de tornar a "ensopegar amb la pedra del franquisme" :

Els nets dels exiliats del franquisme no podran votar i els nets del règim franquista sí?

A més, fonts del PSOE han afirmat que "en una democràcia, el dret de vot no es prohibeix, es garanteix", i han assenyalat PP i Vox dient que "fa anys que demanen eleccions i ara el que volen és que la gent no voti".

El ministre de l'Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska , s'ha expressat en el mateix sentit en una conversa informal amb periodistes durant la recepció oficial del 12 d'Octubre : "Sembla que el dret de vot no és tan rellevant per a alguns", ha dit.

En canvi, el líder del PP, Alberto Núñez Feijóo , ha celebrat la resolució del Suprem, que considera que "ha tornat a posar límits a la irresponsabilitat del govern ". I ha valorat:

El primer en democràcia és complir les regles; en unes eleccions no pot haver-hi dubtes sobre el cens.

També ho ha celebrat Vox, que ho considera una "victòria judicial gegant" davant el govern de Pedro Sánchez. El líder del partit, Santiago Abascal , ha afirmat que les eleccions del 29N es podran celebrar així " sense frau ni alteracions del cens".

Fa un mes, els magistrats van estimar parcialment una petició de Vox i el partit Iustitia Europa i van suspendre provisionalment la inscripció al cens dels milers de descendents d'exiliats de la Guerra Civil que han obtingut el passaport espanyol gràcies a l'última llei de memòria democràtica.
sources.headline: El Suprem manté la suspensió del vot el 29N per a milers de nacionalitzats per la llei de nets

sources.body: <p>A tres días de que se cierre el plazo para el registro de coaliciones a las elecciones generales, los partidos de la izquierda siguen tensando la cuerda. Si el lunes a última hora IU, Comuns, Más Madrid y Movimiento Sumar <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-frente-amplio-propone-a-ada-colau-como-candidata-a-la-presidencia-y-deja-abierta-la-integracion-de-podemos.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-12/el-frente-amplio-propone-a-ada-colau-como-candidata-a-la-presidencia-y-deja-abierta-la-integracion-de-podemos.html">elegían a Ada Colau como candidata </a>y dejaban la puerta abierta a la integración de Podemos en su Frente Amplio, el partido de Belarra, que anunció horas antes un acuerdo de colaboración con ERC, ha tratado de darle la vuelta a la oferta. “Toda la gente que se quiera sumar, bienvenida”, ha señalado Belarra en rueda de prensa este martes, tratando de subrayar la supuesta fortaleza de la entente con los catalanes.</p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/elecciones-generales/2026-10-13/montero-confirma-conversaciones-con-el-frente-amplio-lo-importante-es-llegar-a-buen-puerto.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

sources.body: Queden només tres dies per a la data límit: divendres, 16 d’octubre. Termini perquè els partits que vagin en coalició a les eleccions generals del 29-N comuniquin les seves aliances i, ara com ara, encara hi ha dubtes sobre quines formacions acabaran integrant el Front Ampli , liderat per l’exalcaldessa Colau. També et pot interessar Pedro Sánchez convoca eleccions generals el 29 de novembre després del no als decrets d’habitatge Jaume Planagumà Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura L’origen del Front Ampli A principis d’any, Moviment Sumar , Esquerra Unida ( IU ), Més Madrid i Comuns (les formacions que a les últimes generals es van presentar sota el paraigua de Sumar) van anunciar que confluirien plegades a les generals i van estendre la mà a altres partits com Podem per fer pinya. Just en un moment en què també el portaveu d’ ERC al Congrés, Gabriel Rufián , llançava una proposta: que totes les esquerres anessin a l’una per combatre la dreta i l’ extrema dreta . Fragmentació de les esquerres Més de mig any després i a les portes de les generals, però, la banda esquerra al PSOE segueix fragmentada i aquesta gran aliança no s’ha acabat materialitzant. D’una banda hi ha el Front Ampli de Sumar i, de l’altra, Podem i ERC , que han arribat a un acord de col·laboració sense el Front Ampli. Aquest acord preveu que Podem no es presentarà a Catalunya, però ERC (amb Rufián com a cap de llista) integrarà a la seva candidatura persones de l’entorn de la formació morada. I, a més, Rufián farà actes de campanya fora de Catalunya junt amb Irene Montero . També et pot interessar El clima electoral per l’avançament de les generals es cola a l’Ajuntament de Barcelona Roger Torres i Liñán 2 minuts de lectura Malestar al Front Ampli Tot plegat ha causat malestar a les files del Front Ampli, que aspirava a tenir la col·laboració tant dels morats com dels republicans i consideren que Rufián lluny d’unificar les esquerres les ha dividides. De fet, la setmana passada, quan Rufián encara no havia confirmat que seria el cap de llista d’ERC, Ada Colau va intentar seduir el republicà perquè liderés el Front Ampli . Per tant, a hores d’ara, el Front Ampli segueix estant integrat única i exclusivament per Moviment Sumar, Esquerra Unida (IU), Més Madrid i Comuns, en espera de saber si finalment arriben a un acord amb Podem, que podria passar, també, per exemple, per anar plegats a les llistes de les circumscripcions més petites i no pas una coalició estatal. Ada Colau, candidata a la presidència Sigui com sigui, després que Más Madrid proposés Ada Colau per liderar la llista del Front Ampli , aquest dilluns al vespre el conjunt de la formació va acordar designar l’exalcaldessa candidata a la presidència del Govern espanyol . En un comunicat, Front Ampli va dir que considera que Colau és qui “millor pot assumir el lideratge en la situació política actual” i també van insistir Podem a incorporar-se en el projecte, tot fent una crida a la unitat de totes les esquerres. sources.body:
EL PERIÓDICO ofrece en este directo la última hora de la movilidad en Barcelona y Catalunya .

Sigue en tiempo real el estado del tráfico, las principales retenciones en las carreteras, las incidencias en Rodalies y los retrasos en los trenes AVE entre Barcelona y Madrid , así como las afectaciones al resto del transporte público.

Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona (TMB) aumentará la oferta de metro en las líneas L1 y L5 a partir de este jueves 15 de octubre para reducir los tiempos de espera ante el aumento de pasajeros. La medida supondrá la incorporación de dos trenes adicionales los sábados , entre las 10.00 y las 21.00 horas, y de otro convoy en la L5 durante la hora punta de las tardes de entre semana .

Con el refuerzo, los intervalos de paso los sábados se reducirán en ambas líneas. En la L1, pasarán de más de seis minutos a entre cinco minutos y medio y cuatro minutos y medio, según la franja horaria. En la L5, los intervalos también se acortarán y bajarán de los seis minutos en algunas franjas, hasta situarse por debajo de los cinco minutos durante la tarde.

La medida responde al aumento de la demanda: las validaciones de los sábados en las franjas reforzadas han crecido cerca de un 10% en la L1 y casi un 15% en la L5 entre 2023 y 2026, informa TMB

Un camión que ha chocado contra la mediana obliga a cortar dos carriles de la AP-7 en sentido sur, hacia Barcelona, y otro en sentido norte, hacia Girona, a la altura de Fogars de la Selva.

El accidente provoca retenciones de 5 kilómetros en sentido Barcelona y de 3 kilómetros en sentido Girona.

Fuentes de Renfe confirman que el tren AVE que se incendió este lunes entre Ricla y Plasencia de Jalón (Zaragoza) n o podrá ser retirado hasta "los próximos días" . Una vez retirado el convoy, Adif aún tendrá que arreglar los cables afectados por el fuego que quedaron suspendidos y dar por seguro el tramo. Hasta entonces, los trenes del corredor de alta velocidad tendrán que seguir circulado por vía única en un tramo de más de 20 kilómetros, lo que seguirá provocando retrasos en la alta velocidad entre Barcelona Y Madrid.

La AP-7 presenta complicaciones de tráfico este martes en varios puntos de Catalunya. En sentido Girona, una avería obliga a cortar un carril entre el Papiol y Martorell, donde se registran 9 kilómetros de congestión.

Además, dos accidentes afectan a la circulación a la altura de Fogars de la Selva. En sentido Tarragona, hay 6,3 kilómetros de retenciones entre Fogars de la Selva y Maçanet de la Selva, mientras que en sentido Girona se acumulan 2,7 kilómetros de colas entre Fogars de la Selva y Sant Feliu de Buixalleu. En ambos tramos hay un carril cortado.

En sentido Tarragona también se registran 2 kilómetros de retenciones entre Barberà del Vallès y Santa Perpètua de Mogoda.

La circulación en la A-2 a la altura de Sant Vicenç dels Horts ha recuperado la normalidad tras el corte de un carril provocado por un autobús averiado.

Un autobús averiado obliga a cortar un carril de la A-2 a la altura de Sant Vicenç dels Horts. La incidencia provoca afectaciones al tráfico, aunque la información facilitada no especifica el sentido de la circulación.

sources.body: El metro incrementarà l’oferta a les Línies 1 i 5 a partir del 15 d’octubre , amb l’objectiu de reduir la freqüència de pas a cinc minuts els dissabtes. D’aquesta manera, s’incorporen dos trens addicionals els dissabtes entre les 10 del matí i les 21 h. A més, la Línia 5 també afegeix un tren més durant l’hora punta de la tarda dels dies feiners. Segons TMB, “l’increment d’oferta permetrà reduir els temps d’espera i augmentar la capacitat de transport en dues de les línies més utilitzades de la xarxa”. També et pot interessar TMB sumarà 39 trens per proveir de combois l’L9 i millorar la freqüència a totes les línies Jordi Escofet 3 minuts de lectura Augment de la demanda el cap de setmana Segons TMB, aquest reforç respon a l ‘augment de la demanda que han experimentat les dues línies durant els darrers anys. A l’ L1 , les validacions dels dissabtes a les hores que es reforcen han passat de 215.522 l’any 2023 a 236.400 l’any 2026, amb un increment de prop del 10 % . A l’ L5 , en la franja horària reforçada, les validacions dels dissabtes han crescut de 174.797 a 200.282, és a dir, gairebé un 15 % més . Amb aquest canvi, la freqüència de pas a l’L1 els dissabtes passarà d’intervals superiors als sis minuts a valors d’entre cinc minuts i 30 segons i quatre minuts i 46 segons en funció de la franja horària. A l’L5, els intervals es reduiran des de prop de sis minuts fins a situar-se per sota dels cinc minuts a partir de l’hora amb menys afluència de passatgers. stories.headline: Vall d'Hebron pioneers a minimally invasive treatment for blocked portal veins in children

sources.body: (ACN) L’Hospital Universitari Vall d’Hebron ha aconseguit desobstruir la vena que transporta la sang de l’intestí i la melsa cap al fetge en 12 dels 24 infants tractats des del 2018, mitjançant una tècnica pionera que evita haver de practicar una cirurgia oberta. La vena porta és l’encarregada de transportar la sang procedent de l’intestí i la melsa cap al fetge, on es filtren i processen diverses substàncies. Quan aquesta vena queda obstruïda per un coàgul, la sang no pot circular amb normalitat i busca camins alternatius. Això provoca un augment de la pressió sanguínia, conegut com a hipertensió portal, que pot comportar un engrandiment de la melsa, una disminució de les plaquetes i l’aparició de varius a l’esòfag i l’estómac que poden acabar provocant hemorràgies greus. També et pot interessar El Vall d’Hebron desenvolupa un sistema per alliberar quimioteràpia localitzada menys tòxica Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura Una obstrucció que apareix al cap dels anys El cap de secció d’Hepatologia i Trasplantament Hepàtic Pediàtric de Vall d’Hebron, Jesús Quintero , explica que aquesta obstrucció pot passar desapercebuda durant anys i manifestar-se per primera vegada a la preadolescència o l’adolescència, habitualment entre els 10 i els 15 anys, quan es produeix una hemorràgia digestiva. L’hospital disposa actualment d’un protocol de seguiment amb ecografies dels nadons als quals s’ha col·locat un catèter umbilical per detectar possibles trombosis abans que provoquin complicacions. Dues punxades en lloc d’una cirurgia abdominal Fins ara, una de les principals alternatives per restablir la circulació sanguínia era una intervenció quirúrgica complexa , coneguda com a derivació de Rex, que consisteix a crear una via perquè la sang arribi al fetge. El cirurgià pediàtric José Andrés Molino ha explicat que aquestes operacions requereixen obrir l’abdomen i, en alguns casos, extreure una vena d’una altra part del cos del pacient per construir aquesta connexió. Són intervencions de diverses hores, amb un risc important de sagnat, que habitualment comporten uns dies a la unitat de cures intensives i almenys una setmana d’hospitalització. L’alternativa utilitza tècniques de radiologia intervencionista . Segons ha explicat la cap de secció d’aquesta especialitat al Vall d’Hebron, Mercedes Pérez, els metges fan dues petites punxades, una a través de la melsa i una altra a través del fetge. Amb l’ajuda d’imatges radiològiques introdueixen uns tubs molt fins, anomenats catèters, fins a arribar a la vena obstruïda. Un cop localitzada, intenten reobrir-la amb petits balons i hi col·loquen una pròtesi metàl·lica, coneguda com a stent, que ajuda a mantenir el pas de la sang. El procediment dura habitualment entre dues i tres hores i requereix anestèsia general, però evita les grans incisions de la cirurgia convencional. La meitat dels pacients eviten passar pel quiròfan Des del 2018, el Vall d’Hebron ha tractat 24 pacients d’entre un any i mig i 18 anys , amb una edat mitjana de vuit anys. La tècnica ha permès reobrir la vena porta en 12 casos i, d’aquests, 10 mantenen actualment la vena oberta. Pérez ha reconegut que el percentatge global d’èxit, del 50 %, pot semblar modest, però ha subratllat que significa que un de cada dos infants pot evitar una operació complexa. A més, ha explicat que els resultats estan millorant amb l’experiència i que en alguns dels casos més recents ja s’estan assolint percentatges d’èxit de fins al 70 %. L’hospital rep pacients d’altres comunitats autònomes, ja que es tracta d’una patologia poc freqüent que requereix equips altament especialitzats. Una pacient que va tornar a fer vida normal l’endemà La María José és una pacient que va ser tractada al Vall d’Hebron després de patir una hemorràgia digestiva als 12 anys. La noia, que viu al País Basc, no havia presentat cap símptoma fins que va començar a vomitar grans quantitats de sang, una situació que ha explicat que la va espantar molt. Després de ser atesa inicialment a Vitòria i posteriorment a l’Hospital de Cruces, a Bilbao, va ser derivada al Vall d’Hebron per rebre el tractament. El seu pare, Alexander Correa, ha explicat que la recuperació va ser pràcticament immediata i que l’endemà de la intervenció ja es trobava bé. Des d’aleshores, la jove ha pogut fer vida normal i no ha patit més complicacions, tot i que continua prenent medicació anticoagulant. També et pot interessar Vall d’Hebron realitza el primer trasplantament entre dues persones amb VIH a tot l’estat Sandra García Prat 1 minut de lectura
sources.headline: Una tècnica pionera de Vall d’Hebron permet desobstruir una vena del fetge en infants sense cirurgia
